rules.statement: Each peripheral must specify clocking via a nonempty list of clocking items, each defining clock and reset in fields named clock and reset.

rules.condition: When there are several clocking items
rules.statement: Exactly one clocking item dictionary should have boolean field primary set to true.
The primary clock is used to clock any device interfaces.
Resets within the design are asynchronous active low: assertion is asynchronous to any clock, deassertion is synchronized to the clock of the associated storage element.
Security sensitive storage elements need special care, e.g. synchronous reset after chip-wide reset to a randomized value.

rules.condition: For blocks that generate clocks or resets
rules.statement: The clock and reset fields of a clocking item are optional.
The primary clock item must have both clock and reset fields.
Tradeoff notes on asynchronous active low versus synchronous active high reset are informative only.
Peripherals can connect to the chip bus.
Every peripheral must expose at least one device interface on the chip bus.
Peripherals can act as bus host on some occasions, though the processor being primary host is preferred.
The bus_interfaces attribute should contain a list of dictionaries describing the interfaces the peripheral exposes.
The peripheral must have protocol of tlul since all peripherals use TL-UL.
Each bus interface entry must contain a direction of either host or device.
All bus hosts must use the same clock as the defined primary host clock.

rules.condition: When another entry in the list has the same direction
rules.statement: The name field must be provided to avoid port name collisions.
An entry may include a name, which is added as a prefix to the module's top-level port names.
All lowRISC peripheral designs must conform to the register specification.
All interrupts shall have common naming, hardware interfaces, and software interfaces.

rules.condition: For each name in the interrupt list
rules.statement: The module must have an output named intr_name_o for each interrupt name.
Wired CIP interrupts use active-high level-triggering.
Each interrupt_list entry must have a required name key of type string.
Each interrupt_list entry may have an optional desc string.
Each entry may have an optional type, Event or Status, defaulting to Event if unspecified.
A peripheral generates a separate wired interrupt for each interrupt source.
Peripherals do not send a single combined interrupt for the processor to disambiguate by querying the peripheral.
INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST registers are created at the top of the address map in that order, one bitfield per interrupt.
The .hjson must not define more than 32 interrupts per peripheral.
INTR_STATE at offset 0x0 holds interrupt state, INTR_ENABLE at 0x4 masks it to intr_o, INTR_TEST at 0x8 is write-only and asserts the interrupt.
INTR_STATE shows raw latched interrupt events and is not qualified by INTR_ENABLE.
A designer may choose between Event and Status interrupt behaviors.
The interrupt is cleared only by a software W1C write of the INTR_STATE bitfield.
When the event occurs it is latched into the INTR_STATE bitfield and intr_o is latched high until acknowledged, then low.
prim_intr_hw parameterized with .IntrT("Event") can generate Event interrupt hardware.

rules.condition: Status type interrupt, input persistently true
rules.statement: Interrupt requests are triggered while input is true, including immediately after the previous request is acknowledged.
Designers may generate interrupts from instantaneous events or persistent status, making software handlers simpler and race-free.
